newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian troops return fire in first Albania attack.
newsitem.headline: Italian troops return fire in first Albania attack.

text.p: Three armed men attacked an Italian military camp in southern Albania early on Sunday in the first direct assault on an eight-nation protection force assigned in the Balkan state, a military spokesman said.
Lieutenant Colonel Giovanni Bernardi said the men opened fire on the San Marco camp at the port of Vlore at about 2 a.m. The camp houses 200 Italians from a marine regiment.
"The men on duty fired back into the air in the general proximity of the criminals without trying to kill them," Bernardi told Reuters.
"The criminals quickly disappeared. No one was injured and there was no damage.
"We imagine the criminals wanted to test the reactions and capabilities of the multinational protection force."

Over the past three weeks, 6,000 soldiers from Italy, France, Greece, Turkey, Spain, Denmark, Austria, and Romania have started to arrive in Albania on a United Nations approved mission to oversee the safe delivery of humanitarian aid.
Under the three-month mandate given to the Italian-led force, the troops are not in Albania to act as police or restore law and order to unruly areas.
"We are not here to be Albania's internal police," Bernardi said.

Law and order have become a grave problem since February when Albanians, angered over the loss of savings when five high-risk savings funds collapsed, took to the streets to demand the resignation of the president and their money back.
In the chaos as police and army fled, Albanians raided state arsenals, spreading up to one million guns across the 3.4 million population.
An estimated 700 people have died since early February, killed by criminals, in revenge attacks, or shot accidentally by inexperienced gun-handlers.
Armed gangs are active in many Albanian towns, particularly in the more prosperous south that was hardest hit by the funds fiasco, with poorly equipped police unable to stop them.
